member_subdivisions: Uzbekistan: Bukhara, Jizzakh, Navoiy, Qashqadaryo, Samarkand, Sirdaryo, Surxondaryo, Tashkent Region, Khorazm, Tashkent City
notes: ⚠️ Samarkand and Bukhara are historically major Tajik/Persian cultural centers, not exclusively Uzbek ones, per the frameworks survey's own explicit, 'sometimes politically sensitive' flag (§1) — no longer marked with a distinct hatch on the map itself since the 2026-09-29 solid-color cleanup (every region now renders as one flat color; see this file's own README/STATUS tracker note), but the caveat stays documented here, not smoothed over. ✅ SETTLED 2026-09-28: Uzbekistan (including Samarkand/Bukhara/Surxondaryo/Qashqadaryo regions) stays as current whole territory for now — real research confirmed the disputed 70%/90% Tajik-majority claims for Samarkand and Bukhara are specifically city-core phenomena (official Bukhara Region figure is ~60,898 Tajiks out of ~2M total; Samarkand Region is 63% rural with Tajik concentration confined to the city's historic eastern core), not whole-region majorities — the same shape as Osh city sitting inside a majority-Kyrgyz Osh Region. Surxondaryo has an above-average but still clearly minority Tajik share (12.5% vs. 83% Uzbek). ⚠️ FLAGGED FOR FUTURE DEVELOPMENT, NOT BUILT: the author's own scenario — once Moscow's influence (real, historically coercive: Tajiks in Bukhara reportedly could not get an internal passport without registering as Uzbek) is gone, roughly the first half of the First Interwar Period could plausibly see severe Tajik-Uzbek violence escalating out of this same underlying grievance, potentially producing partial district-level breakaways from Uzbekistan to Tajikistan — most likely candidates being specific districts within Samarkand and Bukhara regions (city and near-city districts), not the regions wholesale. Not designed or dated — a real, sourced-enough premise for a future session to build out, the same way Thailand's Deep South insurgency was eventually turned into a designed post-2083 independence outcome. See frameworks survey's own Samarkand/Bukhara census-manipulation sourcing for the historical grounding (1920 census: 44,758 Tajiks/3,301 Uzbeks in Samarkand city; 1926 census, same city: 43,364 Uzbeks/10,716 Tajiks). ✅ RENAMED 2026-09-29: region_id/name changed from 'uzbek_oasis'/'The Uzbek Oasis Civilization' to 'uzbekistan'/'Uzbekistan' — author's own instruction, same as the other Central Asia renames above. As with Persia/the Kingdom of Nejd and Hejaz on the Middle East map, this real country name doesn't need to cover literally every square kilometer administratively belonging to Uzbekistan — Karakalpakstan and Fergana Valley (Uncertain Territory)'s own Uzbekistani provinces (Fergana, Andijan, Namangan) stay their own distinctly-named/colored regions for the real ethnic/autonomy reasons documented in their own rows, exactly the way Khuzestan and Balochistan stay split out from Persia. Color and member subdivisions unchanged.

✅ SETTLED 2026-09-28: stays part of Uzbekistan as an officially recognized Autonomous Zone — not independent, not ordinary undifferentiated territory. Kept as its own distinctly-colored region, not folded into Uzbekistan's own core region, reflecting a genuinely distinct Turkic ethnicity (closer to Kazakh than Uzbek) and real constitutional autonomy. Historical grounding: created 1925 inside Kazakh jurisdiction, transferred to the Uzbek SSR only in 1936 (late Soviet delimitation, not an organic fit); declared 'sovereignty' in 1990 during the Soviet collapse, traded for a 20-year independence-referendum promise in 1993 that was never honored; ~30 years of quiet compliance followed, propped up by elite continuity and the absence of any outside patron (unlike Transnistria/Abkhazia's Russian backing) rather than by settled harmony; ruptured once in 2022 when Tashkent tried to formally strip the dormant secession clause, triggering the largest unrest in its post-Soviet history (Uzbek government count ~18-21 dead). Author's own reasoning: no active conflict or separatist movement at present, so no reason to change an already-functioning autonomous arrangement — same as leaving a working system alone rather than fixing what isn't currently broken. The underlying props that kept it quiet (elite continuity, no external backer) are flagged as fragile in a post-collapse setting specifically, but not treated as grounds to preemptively change its status here. Not renamed 2026-09-29 alongside its neighbors — 'Karakalpakstan' already is the region's own real, current name (an autonomous republic, not a sovereign country needing a 'cultural label vs. real name' fix).

member_subdivisions: Tajikistan: Khatlon, Districts of Republican Subordination, Sughd, Dushanbe (core); Gorno-Badakhshan/GBAO (domain — lighter shade)
notes: The region's one non-Turkic titular nationality, tracing to the Samanid dynasty (875-999) and the 11th-century ethnonym split from nomadic Turkic groups (frameworks survey §3.5). GBAO's Pamiri population is linguistically and ethnically distinct from lowland Tajik — until the 2026-09-29 solid-color cleanup this was shown as a lighter-shade domain variant within the same region; the map itself now renders the whole region as one flat color, but the distinction stays documented here, not erased. ⚠️ **Sughd settled as core Tajik territory, 2026-09-28** (author decision, following real research): despite sitting geographically inside the Fergana Valley system, Sughd is 84% Tajik / 14.8% Uzbek (2010 census) — decisively majority Tajik, unlike Kyrgyzstan's Osh/Jalal-Abad/Batken, which stayed in Fergana Valley (Uncertain Territory) instead. Sughd is also Tajikistan's economic engine (~60.8% of national industrial output, ~two-thirds of GDP, 2026 figures) and was specifically transferred from the Uzbek SSR to the Tajik SSR in 1929 for exactly the same economic-viability logic that gave Kyrgyzstan Osh/Jalal-Abad in 1924 — except here the demographic majority (84% Tajik) actually supports the assignment, rather than overriding it. A real Uzbek minority and real north/south political friction persist (the Khujand/'Leninabadi' elite ran Tajikistan's government for nearly 40 years, from WWII to the 1992-97 civil war, then was deliberately excluded from power by the postwar settlement) — noted as ongoing internal tension, not grounds for a different territorial assignment. See frameworks survey §2.1/§3.5 for full sourcing. ✅ RENAMED 2026-09-29: region_id/name changed from 'persianate_tajik'/'The Persianate Tajik Highlands' to 'tajikistan'/'Tajikistan' — author's own instruction, same as the other Central Asia renames above. This is the cleanest of the five renames: all five of Tajikistan's real provinces (Khatlon, DRS, Sughd, Dushanbe, GBAO) are already fully contained in this one region, a complete match with no split-out pieces. Color and member subdivisions unchanged.
